name: Cryptic Splice Site Blocking
therapeuticGoalDescription: Restore normal pre-mRNA splicing by masking a pathogenic cryptic splice donor or acceptor site and promoting use of the authentic splice site.
molecularDefect: Mutations create or strengthen cryptic splice donor/acceptor sites, resulting in aberrant exon truncation, exon extension, or abnormal exon inclusion.
diseaseMechanism: The spliceosome preferentially recognizes a cryptic splice site instead of the authentic splice site, producing an abnormal transcript. Steric-blocking ASOs prevent recognition of the cryptic site, allowing restoration of normal splicing.
suitableVariantTypes: Cryptic splice-site variants; deep intronic variants activating cryptic splice sites; exonic or intronic variants that alter splice-site selection.
typicalDiseases: β-thalassemia (HBB); Stargardt disease (ABCA4); Cystic fibrosis (CFTR); Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1); several inherited retinal and neuromuscular disorders with cryptic splice-site mutations.
rnaTargetRegion: Cryptic splice donor site; cryptic splice acceptor site; adjacent splice-regulatory sequences within pre-mRNA.
transcriptRequirement: Presence of a validated pathogenic cryptic splice site whose masking restores normal splicing.
asoChemistry: RNase H-independent steric-blocking ASOs; commonly 2′-O-methyl phosphorothioate (2′-OMe PS), PMO, and related splice-switching chemistries.
typicalLength: Approximately 18–25 nucleotides, depending on target sequence and chemistry.
designRules: Literature synthesis: design ASOs complementary to the cryptic splice site or nearby splice-regulatory elements; avoid RNase H activation; experimentally verify restoration of normal splicing by RT-PCR and sequencing.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible pre-mRNA regions surrounding the cryptic splice site are preferred to facilitate efficient ASO binding.
offTargetConsiderations: Potential unintended modulation of normal alternative splicing in partially complementary transcripts; transcriptome-wide splice analysis is recommended.
advantages: Corrects disease-causing aberrant splicing while preserving endogenous gene regulation; highly mutation-specific; reversible.
limitations: Applicable only to mutations that activate cryptic splice sites; requires precise molecular diagnosis and transcript characterization; repeated administration required.
clinicalTrialExamples: QR-1011 (ABCA4, investigational); several mutation-specific splice-correction programs in inherited retinal disorders and β-thalassemia remain under investigation.

evidenceLevel.note: Strong mechanistic evidence and multiple preclinical/early clinical studies, but no approved therapy specifically for this mechanism.
